channel.title: Pier & Point · UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision (Mission Bay), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois St is the block 33 building between Third St and Illinois St, not the pair of buildings east of Illinois St that this project had listed under that name. The City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside the block 33 outline; UCSF's 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'; SF YIMBY places the facility 'along 3rd Street, immediately across from the UCSF Medical Center'; and the two buildings east of Illinois St were already standing, about six stories tall, in the City's 2010 building survey. The block 33 record is renamed 'UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision' and now carries the 2017 Regents approval, the November 2020 opening, the $237 million cost, the SmithGroup design, the 347,500 sq ft size and the Caffe Central tenant. Its old page address redirects to the new one.

item.title: Correction · UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision: The block 33 record said its identification as UCSF's Valley Center for Vision had no published source. UCSF's June 2025 CAC presentation (map updated December 2024) labels block 33 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)', so the summary, caveat and map notes now cite it, along with OCII's 2019 Land Use Map. Because UCSF's map places the name on block 33, between Third St and Illinois St, the separate 490/499 Illinois St record east of Illinois St may be the one that is mislabelled; that record has not been changed and the question remains open. The record's own mapping log is now labelled as this project's narrative, the NAIP aerial credit names the USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, and the Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural.

item.title: Planned · UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision: UC Regents approve a $237,000,000 project budget and design for UCSF's new Center for Vision Neurosciences building at Mission Bay, which UCSF calls 'Block 33', combining the Department of Ophthalmology and the Francis I. Proctor Foundation in a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and 3-story north wing; construction was expected to begin June 2017 with completion targeted for July 2019 (Jan 26, 2017)
item.description: UC Regents approve a $237,000,000 project budget and design for UCSF's new Center for Vision Neurosciences building at Mission Bay, which UCSF calls 'Block 33', combining the Department of Ophthalmology and the Francis I. Proctor Foundation in a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and 3-story north wing; construction was expected to begin June 2017 with completion targeted for July 2019 (Jan 26, 2017). Source: UC San Francisco, 2017-02.
